problems: CONCURRENT KERNEL WRITERS: another agent that is not in my parallel list wrote kernel/src/core/sched, kernel/src/core/mm, kernel/src/core/fs and kernel/src/blkio during this run. I did not touch those folders. My code imports only sched/control-block.ts (the CTL helpers) and the types in mm/types.ts (PTE, ProcMemStats, used in the PCB). Their tests failed at times while they were being written; at the end everything is green.

C16 FLAGS FLIPPED: during this run every dsa structure's IMPLEMENTED flag changed from false to true (someone implemented all 9). This contradicts the task's instruction. My code switches on the flags, so it now uses the team structures: PidTable for the process table, RingBuffer for klog, dsa/dag in svcmgr, and hashtable plus zorder in the compositor. The marked stand-ins remain behind TODOs (MapProcessTable, ArrayRing, the fallbackPlan relaxation with its 'dsa/dag not implemented — using fallback order' WARN, MapWindowTable, ArrayStackOrder), and tests cover both branches.

valibot is not a dependency of kernel or services, so neither can import it. The dispatcher and V1 validation call schema['~run']({value}, {abortEarly: true}), which is exactly what v.safeParse does in valibot 1.x (kernel/src/core/ipc/parse.ts, services/src/validate.ts, TODO(R1)/TODO(R5)).
The task asked for 'klog.read', but the protocol registry names that call `dmesg`, so it is implemented as `dmesg`. Entries about other users' processes are root-only.

Missing from protocol, declared locally with TODO(protocol): the router-port messages (kernel/src/host/router-protocol.ts), the compositor-port messages (wm/src/compositor/types.ts), the executor frames loaded/killed/error (runtime/executor.ts), TransitionReason, and BuildIdentity (spec protocol/src/identity.ts).

The ai agent's local hook shapes in ai/src/hooks.ts (prefetch, needsConfirmation, semsearch) differ from the architecture §4.4 shapes that @plotinium/kernel/hooks now exports (onIdle/residencyHint, available()). The ai agent needs to reconcile.

web cannot use the compositor yet. wm/package.json exports only '.', and wm/src/index.ts (owned by the UI workflow) exports only PACKAGE_NAME. web therefore mounts a placeholder desktop and hands only the compositor MessagePort to the kernel.

Caddy's CSP `default-src 'self'` blocks the inlined boot `<script>` and `<style>`, which the boot spec requires to be inline. web/dist/csp-hashes.json lists the sha256 sources that ops must add to script-src and style-src.
SELECTORS.md mismatch: tests/e2e/SELECTORS.md expects getByRole('menu', {name: 'Plotinium Boot Manager'}), but the ui/boot menu is a dialog with role listbox. I verified it with the listbox role.

PLACEHOLDER SERVICES: storage, mm, vfs, login and session report RUNNING with a klog WARN 'placeholder service (R2/R3 integration pending)'. auth, sync, lockd, ai.* and complete start DEGRADED with 'not implemented yet' (so sync and ai.indexer show as blocked). Boots always use the built-in manifests because the boot-volume read needs the storage schema. There is no Service Worker yet, so update is degraded.

The kernel timer heap for services is HostTimers, a stand-in that finds the earliest deadline by linear scan and arms one platform timer. It should be replaced by the sched agent's TimerHeap now that dsa/heap is implemented.

Dev-only: the sched budget of 500 ms cannot be met while the Vite dev server transforms the executor's module graph on first request. vite.config.ts defines __PLT_TIMEOUT_SCALE__=20 for `serve` only; release builds keep 1.
No scheduler dispatch loop is wired in the worker yet (core/sched belongs to the other agent). The loopback host has a small deterministic slice driver used only by tests.
The boot-menu 5 s countdown is not implemented, because the allowlisted timer lives in wm/boot-ui/menu.ts, which I do not own. The menu waits for the user.
Coverage in the root vitest config still reports 0/0, as the protocol agent also found. I measured coverage with a temporary config and deleted it afterwards.
todos_for_team: R3 / UI workflow: add `"./compositor": "./src/compositor/index.ts"` to wm/package.json exports, or re-export it from wm/src/index.ts. Then in web/src/main.ts call createCompositor({viewport, insets, raf, interactive, anim, dockIcon}) and bindKernelPort(compositor.port1), and replace the placeholder desktop. Wire WindowFrame props to compositor.titlePointerDown/resizeStart/titleDoubleClick/minimise/restore/toggleMaximise/requestClose. Implement AnimationHooks.play by setting WindowFrame `phase` and resolving on onPhaseEnd.
R1 + R2 + R4: move the router, compositor and executor frame unions, TransitionReason and BuildIdentity into protocol/src/host/* and protocol/src/identity.ts, then import them in kernel and wm.
R1: add valibot (catalog:) to kernel/package.json and services/package.json, and replace the ~run shims with v.safeParse.

R1 / sched agent: attach the scheduler (ready heap, dispatch loop, run tokens, watchdog, kill path) to the kernel worker. Use ProcManager.enterZombie/reparentChildren/reapIfOrphaned and Lifecycle.transition as the proc-side KillHooks. Set ExecPortRec.slice at dispatch, route {t:'syscall'} frames to kernel.execFrame, and replace HostTimers with TimerHeap.

R2: storage/vfs/mm services (replace the placeholders in kernel/src/host/services.ts); the boot-volume read in host/worker.ts onGranted; register the fs syscalls with kernel.handlers.register; install the vfs.*/lock.* visibility hook with kernel.bus.addVisibilityHook; a durable AuditSink (IndexedDB audit store plus outbox).
R3: the login/session services (user wait through ctx.userWait), and the __plt hooks sessionId/layout/terminal in web/src/boot/record.ts.

R4: reconcile ai/src/hooks.ts with @plotinium/kernel/hooks (SchedulerHints, ShellNL, FsSemanticSearch, HookRegistry.register), and register the ai.* handlers. They answer ENOSYS until then, and always in the __AI__=false build.

R5: auth/sync/lockd/update services; sw.ts (vite-plugin-pwa injectManifest) on the router's swRegister; add the web/dist/csp-hashes.json sources to the Caddy CSP; tools/check-boot-truth.ts should scan kernel/src/host/boot-sequence.ts (it has no timers); bootlog/svc.status syscalls on top of ServiceManager.status()/timings()/criticalPath().
Tests owner: fix SELECTORS.md to match the ui boot menu (a dialog with role listbox, named 'Plotinium Boot Manager'), or ask the UI workflow to change the role.
